historical_references.reference: The name 'Israien' appears in some medieval Latin texts as a synonym for 'Syrians' or 'Assyrians'. This usage is likely derived from the Greek term 'Ioudaios' which was used to refer to Jews or people of Judea, and was later applied to non-Jewish Syrians due to their shared use of the Aramaic language and the Old Testament in their liturgy.

The name 'Israien' also appears in some early modern European travel accounts as a reference to the Maronite Christians of Lebanon. These accounts often describe the Maronites as 'Israels' or 'Israelites', reflecting a belief among Europeans that the Maronites were descendants of the ancient Israelites.
